2075945079959853381.owner_posts:
[{"id": "7329842827137778381", "text": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x_8iMEviViY%5D(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v%3Dx_8iMEviViY", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fIO6y_SJw-k", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-21T22:39:49", "expires_at": "2027-03-23T22:39:49", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5147039997625105500", "text": ""I don’t trust producers."

That’s how a well-known director kicked off a shoot with me.

He had every right to be defensive—he’d been burned before by budget notes disguised as creative feedback.

My response was simple: "I'm not here to make your idea smaller. I'm here to make sure it survives the day we shoot it."

Trust on set isn’t built through contracts or written agreements—it’s built through judgment proven again and again in real time.

How do you build trust with new creative partners on high-stakes shoots?", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNnC_wIZcwndTuNTDbybaSvcQBDGli4tw1nezpR=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://weareblend.la/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-18T18:59:27", "expires_at": "2027-03-20T18:59:26", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1389772084650041374", "text": "Blindfolded taste tests in Sawtelle: guessing Japanese dishes behind a RAV4. 🍱

Here’s a look at Challenge ", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOXrjnFxPEzma2AkTEcmmy4wRrBVQDh1DqvmLZI=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://youtu.be/dW3iYa23N3s?si=16z1JHK7-VbvkSkq", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-25T19:58:40", "expires_at": "2027-02-24T19:58:39", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "9135953569178951481", "text": "Blend recently teamed up with DIVE Studios, Intertrend, and Toyota Motor North America to produce "QUEST"—a 25-minute branded challenge series shot across Los Angeles featuring three custom Toyota RAV4 trims.

From format development and game design to multi-cam field production, our team brought this hostless challenge show to life.

Watch the trailer below and check out the full 25-minute episode on YouTube!
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOUQaSuvQHePlC4Ua6usHP8L5EH3-3-1b0qkjdC=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://youtu.be/vmITzGd11DE?si=CrMZpoQZudxpMvIO%5D(https://youtu.be/vmITzGd11DE?si%3DCrMZpoQZudxpMvIO", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-17T18:16:29", "expires_at": "2027-02-16T18:16:27", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5319187627172792431", "text": "True Alignment Over Negotiation

If everyone is winning in different ways, you’re not aligned. You’re negotiating.
The brand, the agency, and the production company all say they want the exact same thing: great work, a strong outcome, and a successful campaign. 

Yet, they rarely measure success the same way:
* Brands look to protect the overall business.
* Agencies focus on protecting the client relationship.
* Production houses work to protect creative execution.

When these priorities pull in opposite directions, the creative itself gets negotiated away. Decisions slow down, safe choices become the default, and endless feedback loops stall momentum.

The Operator Solution
The fix is simple: establish one core operator in the center who owns the outcome across all three fronts. Someone who can accurately translate, decide, and align how everyone wins together.
When you establish unified alignment, the best creative outcome naturally serves the business, strengthens the relationship, and holds execution to the highest standard. That's when projects move fast, and that’s when the work gets better.
Stop negotiating your creative. Align your production.

top_reviews.content:
So first of all let's thank The Misfit down the street for closing down their patio, since that's how we came to be at this gorgeous, high-quality outdoor restaurant for the first time. My partner's parents had offered to fund a nice gift dinner for us, and when our first plan fell through, we set to furiously searching for the perfect steak.

Fortunately, this great little spot absolutely made our night. It's a beautiful glass-walled garden with sofas and chairs and heaters: all the upsides of outdoor dining with none of the downsides.

We started by splitting a salad and a drink, and the staff separated them as a courtesy without being asked. The salad was quite decent in size and construction. The drink got us both pretty sozzled - very generous pour!

Then came the entrees and sides. My partner had the coffee-rubbed ribeye, and I had the salmon, and we shared each other pieces. Both were *amazing*.

Now, some background. I was raised vegetarian, & still eat less meat than average. I don't normally share my partner's taste for beef, but I'll try a bite now and again, and usually just become satisfied that I know my tastes well enough.

This is possibly the first & only time in my life that I've eaten a bite of steak and thought, "I could eat this whole thing. Gosh, wow, I *want* to eat this whole thing." It was juicy and flavorful and a delicate medium-rare texture. I now understand the appeal of steak in a way that I never did before today.

Fortunately, my salmon was also delicious, a generous portion, perfectly cooked, buttery-soft and hearty, with a mild flavor. And all the sides - broccolini, carrots, fingerling potatoes, black rice, an add-on of sautéed mushrooms - were also expertly crafted, and well portioned. So I didn't have to beg my partner for scraps of ribeye like the human golden retriever I am.

Now, I should also mention, she is a truly expert steak connoisseur as only a tiny anemic woman can be, having consumed hundreds of steak dinners over her lifetime. And *she* says it was among the top tier of steaks *she'd* ever had.

We finished off by sharing a perfectly pulled double espresso, to balance out the alcohol.

The staff were all very kind, communicative, and solicitous - I didn't catch everyone's name, but our server was Lily and she was fantastic.

Everyone was knowledgeable and responsive about our allergy concerns, so we had a great, celiac-safe, gluten-free dinner, with many options available.
